scalars.scalar_value: Progressive EVS leadership experience in a complex, 24/7 acute-care healthcare environment.

Five (5) years of successful supervisory and/or management experience demonstrating effective leadership in a large, complex, and/or widely dispersed Environmental Services, custodial, or related services operation, including management experience in a healthcare facility; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

items.item_text: CHESP - Certified Health Care Environmental Services professional certification
Must be able and willing to work various shifts, hours, weekends, holidays, and locations based on operational and business needs.
Must be available to respond to urgent or emergency operational needs as required by departmental responsibilities.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
A Bachelor's Degree in a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Five (5) years of successful supervisory and/or management experience demonstrating effective leadership in a large, complex, and/or widely dispersed Environmental Services, custodial, or related services operation, including management experience in a healthcare facility; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Progressive EVS leadership experience in a complex, 24/7 acute-care healthcare environment.
Supervisory experience in a healthcare facility with working knowledge of human resources management practices and policies.
Experience managing multi-shift EVS and clean linen operations.

Demonstrated experience leading and developing EVS teams, including performance management, quality assurance, environmental rounds, cleaning audits, corrective actions, and accountability for operational, quality, safety, and service standards.
Experience working in a union-represented workforce, with knowledge of collective bargaining agreements and labor-relations practices.
Ability to maintain strict confidentiality with experience applying good judgment and discretion.

Under the direction of the Director of Environmental Services, the Manager of Environmental Services provides operational leadership and oversight for Environmental Services across assigned hospital areas, shifts, and locations. The Manager is responsible for the safe, efficient, and consistent delivery of environmental cleaning, clean linen services, and related support services in support of patient safety, infection prevention, patient flow, regulatory compliance, employee safety, and the overall patient experience.

The EVS Manager oversees day-to-day departmental operations through supervisors, lead custodians, and frontline staff. Responsibilities include staffing and resource allocation; environmental cleaning and disinfection; clean linen inventory, distribution, utilization, and storage management; implementation and administration of departmental policies, procedures, and standards; quality assurance and continuous performance improvement; employee training and competency; equipment and supply management; regulatory readiness; and maintenance of required departmental records and documentation.

The Manager provides leadership, coaching, development, and accountability for EVS supervisors, leads, and staff. Establishes clear performance expectations and ensures consistent application of departmental policies, procedures, work standards, safety practices, and applicable collective bargaining agreements across shifts and locations.

The Manager provides leadership within a diverse, union-represented workforce and participates in personnel and labor-relations activities, including recruitment, selection, onboarding, attendance management, performance evaluations, employee development, investigations, corrective action, discipline, and other employee-relations activities. Partners with Human Resources and Labor/Employee Relations to ensure consistent application of organizational policies, procedures, and labor agreements.

The Manager monitors and evaluates Environmental Services quality assurance and continuous improvement programs. Uses environmental rounds, cleaning audits, and inspection results to identify trends, determine root causes, implement corrective actions, and sustain improvements.
Able to quickly learn operational needs, and work collaboratively on a fast-paced, high-functioning team.

Demonstrated knowledge of healthcare EVS operations, infection prevention, environmental cleaning and disinfection, regulated waste, and applicable CDPH, TJC, CMS, OSHA, and Environment of Care requirements.
Strong communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to effectively engage employees, union representatives, leadership, and clinical partners.
Have a thorough, proven understanding of procedures for the proper handling, storage, and disposal of chemotherapy, infectious/biohazard, pharmaceutical, and confidential waste streams.
Must be proficient with MS Office and Maintenance Management systems.
Strong organizational skills with an independent ability to set priorities and manage conflicting demands with limited supervision.
